mainTopic: How a יבמה is acquired and released: ביאה only, חליצה, the יבם's death, and why a גט and חליצה cannot replace each other
overview: The גמרא brings the פסוק showing that ביאה makes the יבמה the יבם's wife. Using the word 'וְיִבְּמָהּ', it shows that only ביאה completes her acquisition (not כסף or שטר), and that the יבום can happen even against her will. Next comes the source that חליצה frees her to all of ישראל. This is learned from 'בישראל', which is written twice, while the public announcement 'חלוץ הנעל' comes from 'ונקרא שמו'. The גמרא then proves by a קל וחומר from an אשת איש that the יבם's death frees the יבמה, and רב אשי defends it against challenges. It asks why a married woman can't leave through חליצה ('ספר כריתת' blocks it), and why a יבמה can't leave through a גט. The answer 'ככה' is challenged from the goats of יום הכפורים. The גמרא then tries 'לה', and finally settles on 'נעל'. The amud ends with a ברייתא suggesting 'נעל' is needed to include anyone's shoe and to require a shoe that fits. The challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The verse that makes the יבמה a wife through ביאה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק showing that once the יבם has ביאה with the יבמה, she becomes his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Her brother-in-law shall come upon her and take her to him as a wife.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק as the source for the משנה's rule that a יבמה is acquired through ביאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק first says 'יבמה יבא עליה' (he comes upon her) and then 'ולקחה לו לאשה' (he takes her as a wife). The order shows that the ביאה is what turns her into his אשה.

keyTerms.meaning: The widow of a man who died without children, who is tied to his brother
The brother of the man who died, who may marry the widow
Marital relations, which acquire the יבמה
As a wife

phrases.english: "Her brother-in-law shall come upon her
phrases.notes: דברים 25:5

phrases.english: and take her to him as a wife."

steps.triggerLanguage: יְבָמָהּ יָבֹא עָלֶיהָ וּלְקָחָהּ לוֹ לְאִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the משנה's rule (יבמה נקנית בביאה), continuing the discussion from before this section.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that ביאה acquires the יבמה
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 25:5: יבמה יבא עליה ולקחה לו לאשה

steps.title: Maybe she is like a regular wife in every way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if the פסוק calls her 'a wife,' maybe she can also be acquired with כסף or שטר, like any wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that she is like a wife in every respect!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes on the word 'לאשה' and asks whether the יבמה should follow all the rules of a regular wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A regular woman can be married with כסף, שטר, or ביאה. If the פסוק calls the יבמה 'a wife,' maybe all three ways should work for her too, and not only ביאה.

keyTerms.meaning: But say (introduces a different reading)
For every matter, in every respect

phrases.english: But say: she is like a wife in every matter!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the word 'לאשה' in the פסוק reaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implied idea that the יבמה is acquired only through ביאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the פסוק calls her 'a wife,' then all the ways of acquiring a wife (כסף, שטר) should work for her as well.

steps.title: A ברייתא: only ביאה completes her acquisition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea, using a ברייתא that learns from 'וְיִבְּמָהּ' that only ביאה, and not כסף or שטר, completes the acquisition of a יבמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That cannot be, as a ברייתא teaches: You might think money and a document complete her acquisition, the way ביאה does. So the פסוק says 'וְיִבְּמָהּ': ביאה completes her acquisition, but money and a document do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by quoting a ברייתא that says clearly that כסף and שטר do not fully acquire a יבמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the word 'ויבמה' (and he shall do יבום with her) as limiting: only the act of יבום, which is ביאה, completes the acquisition. So 'לאשה' does not mean she is like a wife in every respect.

keyTerms.meaning: It cannot enter your mind; that is not possible
As a ברייתא teaches
Money and a document, two ways of marrying a woman
Complete, finish the acquisition
The פסוק teaches (comes to say)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא says כסף and שטר do not 'complete' the acquisition. It does not say they do nothing at all. The point is only that they cannot finish it the way ביאה does.

phrases.english: It cannot enter your mind, as it is taught:

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל יְהוּ כֶּסֶף וּשְׁטָר גּוֹמְרִים בָּהּ,
phrases.english: One might think money and a document complete her acquisition,
in the way that ביאה completes it?
So the verse says: "And he shall do יבום with her" –
phrases.notes: דברים 25:5

phrases.english: ביאה completes her acquisition,
but money and a document do not complete it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 2 with a ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from a ברייתא that limits the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since she is called 'a wife,' כסף and שטר should work like ביאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'ויבמה' teaches that only ביאה completes the acquisition of a יבמה.

steps.title: Maybe 'וְיִבְּמָהּ' teaches that her consent is not needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the word 'וְיִבְּמָהּ' comes to teach a different law: the יבם may do יבום even against her will.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say: what does 'וְיִבְּמָהּ' teach? That he may do יבום with her against her will.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's use of the word 'ויבמה' by offering another thing that word could be teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'ויבמה' is needed to teach that the יבום works even without her consent, then it is already used up. In that case it cannot also teach that only ביאה completes the acquisition.

keyTerms.meaning: Against her will, without her consent
Performs יבום

phrases.english: But say: what is "and he shall do יבום with her"?
That he may do יבום with her against her will.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how the ברייתא in step 3 reads the word 'ויבמה'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's teaching from 'ויבמה' that only ביאה completes her acquisition
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word may be needed for another law (no consent needed), so it is not free to teach that כסף and שטר do not work.

steps.title: The extra word teaches both laws
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the פסוק could have said just 'וְיִבֵּם.' Writing 'וְיִבְּמָהּ' adds something, so we learn two laws from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the פסוק say 'וְיִבֵּם.' Why does it say 'וְיִבְּמָהּ'? Learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the word 'ויבמה' has extra wording, so it can teach both ideas: no consent is needed, and only ביאה completes her acquisition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To teach that it depends only on him, the פסוק could have said 'ויבם' (and he shall do יבום). The added ending 'ה' (her) points to her and gives an extra teaching. So the word supports both laws.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Let the פסוק say
Learn two things from it

steps.whatToRemember: A יבמה is acquired only through ביאה, not through כסף or שטר, and the יבום can be done even against her will. Both laws come from the word 'וְיִבְּמָהּ.'

phrases.english: If so, let the verse say: "and he shall do יבום,"
Why "and he shall do יבום with her"?
phrases.notes: The extra ending 'ה', meaning 'her', is what the גמרא is pointing to.

phrases.english: Learn two things from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 4 and keeps the ברייתא's reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The extra wording allows two teachings
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ויבמה' only teaches that her consent is not needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The longer form 'ויבמה' teaches both laws: no consent is needed, and only ביאה completes her acquisition.

steps.title: Where do we learn release through חליצה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the next part of the משנה: the יבמה goes free through חליצה. It asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Through חליצה.' From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'בחליצה' and asks for the source. This opens a new topic and sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the יבמה 'acquires herself' (goes free) through חליצה. The גמרא wants a פסוק that shows חליצה releases her to marry anyone.

keyTerms.meaning: The ceremony of removing the יבם's shoe, which frees the יבמה
From where do we know?

phrases.english: "Through חליצה." From where do we derive it?
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: the יבמה goes free through חליצה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the יבם acquiring the יבמה to how the יבמה goes free.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that shows חליצה releases the יבמה

steps.title: The verse 'בית חלוץ הנעל' frees her to all of ישראל
steps.stepSummary: The source is the פסוק 'ונקרא שמו בישראל בית חלוץ הנעל.' Once the shoe is removed, she is permitted to all of ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And his name shall be called in Israel: the house of him whose shoe was removed.' Once the shoe has been removed, she is permitted to all of Israel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 6 with a פסוק about the חליצה ceremony.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'בישראל' is read as saying that after the shoe is removed she is free to marry any Jew. That is how חליצה releases her.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written
The one whose shoe was removed
She became permitted

phrases.english: As it is written: "And his name shall be called in Israel:
phrases.notes: דברים 25:10

phrases.english: the house of him whose shoe was removed" –
once the shoe has been removed by her,
she is permitted to all of Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: וְנִקְרָא שְׁמוֹ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל בֵּית חֲלוּץ הַנָּעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From 'ונקרא שמו בישראל': after חליצה she is permitted to all of ישראל.

steps.title: 'בישראל' is already used for a different teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the word 'בישראל' is needed for רב שמואל בר יהודה's teaching that חליצה must be done in a Jewish בית דין, not a non-Jewish court.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this 'Israel' come for this? It is needed for what רב שמואל בר יהודה taught: 'In Israel' means in a Jewish court, and not in a court of non-Jews!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the word 'בישראל' can teach that she is free to marry anyone, when it is already needed for another law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב שמואל בר יהודה learns from 'בישראל' that חליצה must take place in a Jewish בית דין. If the word is used for that, it seems it cannot also be the source for her being permitted to all of ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that what it comes for?
It is needed for
A court
Non-Jews

phrases.english: Does this "Israel" come for this?
This is needed
for what Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda taught:
"In Israel" – in a court of Jews,
and not in a court of non-Jews!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source given in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: Learning from 'בישראל' that she is permitted to all of ישראל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word is already needed to teach that חליצה must be done in a Jewish בית דין, so it is not free for another teaching.

steps.title: 'בישראל' appears twice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'בישראל' is written twice in the section, so each one teaches a different law.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'In Israel' is written twice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the challenge: there are two mentions of 'בישראל,' one for the Jewish בית דין rule and one for her being permitted to all of ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the word appears twice in the פרשה of יבום, it can carry two separate teachings. So both רב שמואל בר יהודה's law and the release through חליצה have a source.

keyTerms.meaning: Two
Are written

steps.whatToRemember: חליצה frees the יבמה to marry anyone. This is learned from 'בישראל,' which appears twice, so one mention also teaches that חליצה must be done in a Jewish בית דין.

phrases.english: "In Israel" is written twice.
phrases.notes: דברים 25:7 and דברים 25:10

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two mentions of the word, one for each teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'בישראל' teaches only that חליצה must be done in a Jewish בית דין.
steps.terutzMaskana: There are two mentions of 'בישראל': one teaches the Jewish בית דין rule, and the other teaches that she is permitted to all of ישראל.

steps.title: The word 'In Israel' seems needed for another teaching too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: 'בישראל' is also needed for the ברייתא where רבי טרפון had everyone call out 'חלוץ הנעל' after a חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the word 'בישראל' is still needed for what a ברייתא teaches. רבי יהודה said: Once we were sitting before רבי טרפון, and a יבמה came to do חליצה. He told us: All of you answer and say, 'The one whose shoe was removed, the one whose shoe was removed!'
steps.whatsHappening: Step 9 said there were two 'בישראל's, one for each law. Now the גמרא asks whether there is a third law that also needs one of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טרפון had the whole group announce 'חלוץ הנעל', which makes the חליצה public among the Jewish people. That publicity seems to come from the word 'בישראל'. If so, we no longer have a spare 'בישראל' to teach that she is permitted to all of ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: But still
It is needed for
As a ברייתא teaches
The one whose shoe was removed (the title announced after חליצה)

phrases.english: But still, it is needed for that which is taught in a ברייתא:
phrases.notes: 'It' means the word בישראל from the last step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: פַּעַם אַחַת הָיִינוּ יוֹשְׁבִים לִפְנֵי רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן,
phrases.english: Once we were sitting before Rabbi Tarfon,
and a yevama came to perform chalitza,
and he said to us:
All of you, answer and say:
"The one whose shoe was removed, the one whose shoe was removed!"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Renews the challenge to Step 9 by pointing to a third law that may need 'בישראל'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Steps 7 and 9 that a spare 'בישראל' teaches she is permitted to all of ישראל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'בישראל' is also used for publicly announcing the חליצה, the extra word is used up and cannot teach the permission.

steps.title: The announcement comes from 'and his name shall be called'
steps.stepSummary: The public announcement is learned from 'ונקרא שמו', not from 'בישראל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: That law comes from 'and his name shall be called.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי טרפון's announcement is learned from a different phrase in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ונקרא שמו' means a name is called out about him, so announcing 'חלוץ הנעל' comes from those words. 'בישראל' is free again, and the source from Step 7 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is derived from
And his name shall be called

steps.whatToRemember: The two 'בישראל's teach (1) a Jewish בית דין and (2) she is permitted to all of ישראל. The public announcement comes from 'ונקרא שמו'.

phrases.english: That law is derived from "And his name shall be called."
phrases.notes: דברים 25:10. Calling out his new name is exactly what רבי טרפון had them do.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 10 by giving the announcement its own source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the law to a different phrase in the פסוק
steps.terutzMaskana: The announcement comes from 'ונקרא שמו', so 'בישראל' still teaches the permission.

steps.title: Source for the יבמה going free when the יבם dies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the last part of the משנה and asks how we know the יבם's death frees the יבמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And through the death of the יבם.' From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: This opens a new section. The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה and asks for their source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said a יבמה goes free through חליצה or through the יבם's death. חליצה has been sourced. Now the גמרא wants a source for the death of the יבם.

keyTerms.meaning: The death of the brother-in-law
From where do we know?

phrases.english: "And through the death of the yavam."
From where do we derive this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the חליצה clause to the final clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that the יבם's death permits the יבמה to marry anyone.

steps.title: A קל וחומר from a married woman
steps.stepSummary: If a husband's death frees an אשת איש, whose prohibition is חנק, then surely the יבם's death frees a יבמה, whose prohibition is only a לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a קל וחומר. A married woman is forbidden to others under the punishment of חנק, and still her husband's death permits her. A יבמה is forbidden only by a לאו, so all the more so the יבם's death permits her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a קל וחומר, a 'how much more so' argument, comparing a יבמה to a married woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The stricter case, אשת איש (death penalty), still ends with the husband's death. The lighter case, יבמה (only a לאו), should surely end with the יבם's death.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'how much more so' argument from a stricter case to a lighter one
A married woman
Death by strangulation
A plain negative commandment (no death penalty)
Is it not all the more so?

phrases.english: It is an a fortiori inference:
If a married woman, who is forbidden under strangulation,
is permitted by the death of her husband,
then a yevama, who is forbidden only by a prohibition,
is it not all the more so?
phrases.notes: He means: surely the יבם's death permits her.

steps.triggerLanguage: קַל וָחוֹמֶר: וּמָה אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ שֶׁהִיא בְּחֶנֶק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קל וחומר from אשת איש: the stricter prohibition ends with the husband's death, so the lighter one surely ends with the יבם's death.

steps.title: A married woman can also leave with a גט
steps.stepSummary: The קל וחומר is challenged: an אשת איש is more easily released since a גט also frees her, but a יבמה cannot leave with a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a married woman? She can leave with a גט. Will you say the same about this one, who cannot leave with a גט?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the קל וחומר by showing a way an אשת איש is easier to release than a יבמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if the 'strict' case is truly stricter in every relevant way. An אשת איש has an extra way out, a גט, so maybe her bond is looser. Then the comparison to a יבמה breaks.

keyTerms.meaning: What about...? (opens a challenge that shows a difference)
Bill of divorce
Will you say?

phrases.english: What is special about a married woman?
That she can leave through a bill of divorce.
Will you say the same about this one, who does not leave through a bill of divorce?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְאֵשֶׁת אִישׁ, שֶׁכֵּן יוֹצְאָה בְּגֵט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the קל וחומר of Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The קל וחומר from אשת איש to יבמה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An אשת איש has a leniency the יבמה lacks (release by גט), so she is not stricter in every way.

steps.title: A יבמה also has a way out: חליצה
steps.stepSummary: The challenge fails because a יבמה can also be released while the יבם is alive, through חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one also leaves through חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the challenge of Step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חליצה does for a יבמה what a גט does for a wife. It frees her while he is alive. So both have a living way out, and the difference disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: This one also
The shoe-removal ceremony that frees a יבמה

phrases.english: This one also leaves through chalitza.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge of Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the supposed difference also exists in the other case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only an אשת איש can be released while the man is alive.
steps.terutzMaskana: A יבמה can also be released while the יבם is alive, through חליצה, so the קל וחומר stands.

steps.title: For a married woman, the one who forbids her is the one who frees her
steps.stepSummary: A new challenge: with an אשת איש, the husband both forbids her and frees her by dying. A יבמה became forbidden through her husband's death, so it is not the same person.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what about a married woman? The one who forbids her is the one who permits her!
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first challenge failed, the גמרא offers a different difference to break the קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband made her forbidden by marrying her, so it makes sense that his death frees her. A יבמה seems to have been made forbidden by her husband's death, not by the יבם. So why should the יבם's death free her?

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces a new attempt)
The one who forbids her is the one who permits her

phrases.english: Rather: What is special about a married woman?
That the one who forbids her is the one who permits her!
phrases.notes: Her husband forbade her to others by marrying her, and he frees her when he dies.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: מָה לְאֵשֶׁת אִישׁ שֶׁכֵּן אוֹסְרָהּ מַתִּירָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the failed challenge of Step 14 with a new one against the קל וחומר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The קל וחומר from אשת איש to יבמה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With an אשת איש, the same person who created the prohibition removes it. With a יבמה, this seems not to be so.

steps.title: רב אשי: the יבם also forbids her and frees her
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the יבם is the one who forbids the יבמה, since without him she would be free, and he is also the one who frees her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Here too, the one who forbids her permits her. The יבם forbids her, and the יבם permits her.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי shows that the same pattern holds for a יבמה, so the קל וחומר works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What keeps the יבמה forbidden is the living יבם. If there were no יבם, she would be free right away. He also frees her through חליצה. So the יבם forbids her and permits her, just like a husband, and his death frees her by קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the answer here
The brother-in-law
Permits her

steps.whatToRemember: The source that the יבם's death frees the יבמה is a קל וחומר from אשת איש. The challenges fail because the יבמה also has חליצה, and the יבם is also the one who both forbids and permits her.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Here too, the one who forbids her is the one who permits her:
the yavam forbids her,
and the yavam permits her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: הָא נָמֵי אוֹסְרָהּ מַתִּירָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 16, which saves the קל וחומר of Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the supposed difference also exists in the other case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A יבמה is forbidden by her husband's death, not by the יבם, so the pattern does not match.
steps.terutzMaskana: The יבם is the one who forbids her and the one who permits her, so the קל וחומר holds.

steps.title: Why can't a married woman be freed through חליצה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא builds a קל וחומר: a יבמה can't leave with a גט but can leave with חליצה, so an אשת איש, who can leave with a גט, should surely also be able to leave with חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let a married woman also be able to leave her marriage through חליצה, by a קל וחומר. A יבמה cannot leave through a גט, and yet she can leave through חליצה. A married woman can leave through a גט. Isn't it logical that she can also leave through חליצה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the earlier comparison around. It asks why the release method of a יבמה (חליצה) shouldn't also work for a married woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier steps, the גמרא compared the אשת איש and the יבמה to learn how a יבמה goes free. Now it pushes the comparison the other way. If the 'weaker' case (the יבמה, who can't use a גט) can use חליצה, then the 'stronger' case (the אשת איש, who can use a גט) should be able to use it too.

keyTerms.meaning: The ceremony in which the brother-in-law's shoe is removed, which frees a יבמה
A bill of divorce
Isn't it logical? (the classic wording of a קל וחומר)
Leaves, meaning goes free from the bond

phrases.english: And let a married woman leave through חליצה
by a קל וחומר:
If a יבמה, who does not leave through a גט,
leaves through חליצה,
then this one, who does leave through a גט,
is it not logical that she leaves through חליצה?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְהֵא אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ יוֹצְאָה בַּחֲלִיצָה מִקַּל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same אשת איש / יבמה comparison from steps 13-17, but runs it in reverse to ask about the אשת איש.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that an אשת איש can only be freed by a גט or by death.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from the יבמה: she can't use a גט but can use חליצה, so the married woman, who can use a גט, should be able to use חליצה too.

steps.title: Only a written document cuts the marriage
steps.stepSummary: The verse says 'ספר כריתת': only a written document severs a married woman, and nothing else, including חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'a scroll of severance.' This teaches that a scroll cuts her off from her husband, and nothing else cuts her off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by pointing to the תורה's wording about divorce. The wording blocks the קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'ספר כריתת' are read as exclusive. Only a written document (ספר) can cut the marriage while the husband is alive. Since the Torah limits the method, logic can't add חליצה as another way out.

keyTerms.meaning: 'A scroll of severance', the Torah's name for a גט
Cuts her off, meaning severs her from the marriage
The verse says (bringing a verse as proof)

phrases.english: The verse says: "A scroll of severance"
phrases.notes: דברים 24:1

phrases.english: a scroll cuts her off,
and nothing else cuts her off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קל וחומר of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A verse that limits the method blocks the logical inference.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Logic would say an אשת איש could also leave through חליצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah says only a written document severs a marriage, so חליצה does not work for an אשת איש.

steps.title: Why can't a יבמה be freed through a גט?
steps.stepSummary: The reverse קל וחומר: a married woman can't leave with חליצה but can leave with a גט, so a יבמה, who can leave with חליצה, should surely be able to leave with a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let a יבמה be able to leave through a גט, by a קל וחומר. A married woman cannot leave through חליצה, and yet she can leave through a גט. A יבמה can leave through חליצה. Isn't it logical that she can also leave through a גט?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא flips the question. It asks why the married woman's release method (a גט) shouldn't also work for a יבמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 explained why חליצה can't free a married woman. This step asks the mirror question about the יבמה. Since the married woman can't use חליצה but can use a גט, the יבמה, who can use חליצה, should be able to use a גט as well.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow whose husband died without children, who is tied to his brother
By an argument from a lighter case to a stricter one

phrases.english: And let a יבמה leave through a גט
by a קל וחומר:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ שֶׁאֵין יוֹצְאָה בַּחֲלִיצָה –
phrases.english: If a married woman, who does not leave through חליצה,
leaves through a גט,
then this one, who does leave through חליצה,
is it not logical that she leaves through a גט?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְהֵא יְבָמָה יוֹצֵאת בְּגֵט מִקַּל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror image of step 18, now asked about the יבמה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that a יבמה can only be freed by חליצה (or by the יבם's death).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from the married woman: she can't use חליצה but can use a גט, so the יבמה, who can use חליצה, should be able to use a גט too.

steps.title: The word 'ככה' makes חליצה essential
steps.stepSummary: The verse about חליצה says 'ככה' (so shall it be done), and that word makes חליצה the only valid way, so a גט cannot replace it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'so' about חליצה, and the word 'so' means this is essential. It must be done exactly this way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from the word 'ככה' in the verses about חליצה. That word blocks any other method.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the תורה says 'ככה', it means the procedure must be done exactly as described. Nothing can replace it. This עיכובא shuts down the קל וחומר, so a יבמה cannot go free through a גט.

keyTerms.meaning: 'So', meaning exactly this way
Essential; it blocks validity if not done this way

phrases.english: The verse says: "So"
phrases.notes: דברים 25:9

phrases.english: and "so" means it is essential.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קל וחומר of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A word that makes the procedure essential blocks the logical inference.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Logic would say a יבמה could also leave through a גט.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ככה' makes חליצה essential, so a גט does not free a יבמה.
steps.whatToRemember: A married woman goes free only through a גט, because 'ספר כריתת' blocks the קל וחומר that would let חליצה free her. The next steps question whether 'ככה' alone can stop a גט from freeing a יבמה. Step 31 then brings a new source ('נעל'), which step 32 challenges in turn.

steps.title: Does an essential requirement always block a קל וחומר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the idea from step 21 by pointing to יום הכפורים, where the Torah also uses essential wording ('גורל' and 'חוקה').
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it true that whenever there is an essential requirement, we don't learn a קל וחומר? But look at יום הכפורים, where the Torah writes 'lot' and 'statute'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 21. It starts setting up a counter-example from the goats of יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 assumed that once the Torah makes something essential, a קל וחומר can't apply. The גמרא now asks if that is always true. The יום הכפורים service has essential wording too: the word 'חוקה' makes its details essential. The rest of the challenge is built out in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: We learn out, meaning we derive
But look at (opens a counter-example)
The lottery used to choose between the two goats of יום הכפורים
'Statute', a word that makes the details essential

phrases.english: And anywhere there is an essential requirement,
do we not learn a קל וחומר?
But there is יום הכפורים,
where it is written "lot" and "statute",
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:9 and 16:34. 'Statute' tells us the יום הכפורים details are essential.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֹל הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא עִיכּוּבָא לָא דָּרְשִׁי קַל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning used in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle from step 21 that an essential-requirement word blocks a קל וחומר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יום הכפורים also has essential wording, and the case there is used to show that a קל וחומר might still have been considered.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not questioning whether חליצה is required. It is questioning only the general rule that essential wording automatically stops a קל וחומר.

steps.title: The ברייתא: only the lottery makes the goat a חטאת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that on יום הכפורים the lottery makes the goat a חטאת, and simply naming it does not. This sets up the challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a ברייתא teaches: 'And he shall make it a חטאת' teaches that the lottery makes it a חטאת, but naming it does not make it a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as the source for its challenge. It is still setting up the challenge, and the main point comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that on יום הכפורים, the goat becomes a חטאת only through the lottery, and not by a spoken designation. Normally a spoken designation does make an animal a חטאת. So here the Torah had to exclude naming, even though the case also has essential wording. This is the material the גמרא will use against the rule of step 21.

keyTerms.meaning: And a ברייתא teaches
'And he shall make it a חטאת'
The name, meaning a spoken designation of the animal

phrases.english: and it is taught: "And he shall make it a חטאת"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:9

phrases.english: the lottery makes it a חטאת,
but the naming does not make it a חטאת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the ברייתא that supports the challenge opened in step 22.
steps.raayaObject: That even where there is essential wording, the Torah still needed a verse to exclude another method.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on ויקרא 16:9: the lottery makes the goat a חטאת, not a spoken designation.

steps.title: The ברייתא's logical argument: naming should work where a lottery works
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains why a verse was needed. Logic alone would say that naming the goat as a חטאת should work on יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: A verse was needed, because one might have thought: isn't it logical? In places where a lottery does not set aside an offering, simply naming it does. So where a lottery does work, surely naming should work too!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא lays out the קל וחומר it plans to reject. This sets up the verse that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With ordinary offerings, a lottery does nothing, yet naming an animal as a חטאת does make it one. On יום הכפורים, even a lottery can make a חטאת. So the reasoning is that naming should surely work there as well.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it logical? (the opening of a קל וחומר argument)
Lottery, used to choose which goat goes to ה' on יום הכפורים
The naming: saying out loud 'this is a חטאת'
Made holy, set aside for a specific offering

phrases.english: for one might have thought: is it not logical?
If in a place where a lottery does not set aside an offering,
naming it does set it aside,
then in a place where a lottery does set it aside,
is it not logical that naming should set it aside?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the ברייתא from step 23, giving the logic the verse must block.
steps.raayaObject: Showing that a קל וחומר would normally apply on יום הכפורים, even though essential wording is written there
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא on the יום הכפורים goats

steps.title: The verse blocks the logic: only the lottery makes it a חטאת
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא cites 'ועשהו חטאת' to teach that only the lottery, and not naming, makes the goat a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the verse says: 'And he shall make it a sin-offering.' The lottery makes it a חטאת; naming it does not make it a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by bringing a verse that rejects the קל וחומר from step 24.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse limits it: on יום הכפורים, the lottery is what makes the goat a חטאת. Naming alone does nothing. The important point is that a special verse was needed to stop the קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: So the verse teaches (introduces a verse that settles the question)
'And he shall make it a sin-offering' (ויקרא 16:9)

phrases.english: The verse says: 'And he shall make it a sin-offering':
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:9

phrases.english: the lottery makes it a sin-offering,
but naming does not make it a sin-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא by rejecting the קל וחומר of step 24 with a verse.
steps.raayaObject: Only an extra limiting verse stopped the קל וחומר on יום הכפורים

steps.title: Essential wording does not block a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The verse was only needed because a קל וחומר would otherwise apply, even with 'חוקה' written there. So 'ככה' should not block the קל וחומר for חליצה either.
steps.simpleTranslation: The only reason naming fails is that the verse excluded it. Without that verse, we would have learned the קל וחומר, even though 'חוקה' is written there!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the lesson from the ברייתא and uses it to challenge the answer from step 21.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 said that 'ככה' makes חליצה the only way, so a קל וחומר cannot add a גט. But on יום הכפורים, 'חוקה' is written and a special verse was still needed to block the קל וחומר. So essential wording by itself does not stop a קל וחומר, and the reverse קל וחומר from step 20 comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: That the verse excluded it
But if not for this (the verse)
We would learn out / derive
'A statute': wording that marks a law as essential and fixed

phrases.english: And the reason is that the verse excluded it;
but if not for that,
we would learn the קל וחומר,
even though 'statute' is written there!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְטַעְמָא דְּמַעֲטֵיהּ קְרָא, הָא לָאו הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the ברייתא in steps 23-25 to attack step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 21 that 'ככה' blocks the reverse קל וחומר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: On יום הכפורים, 'חוקה' did not block the קל וחומר; only an extra limiting verse did. So 'ככה' alone cannot block a גט for a יבמה.

steps.title: 'לה' in the גט verse: for her, not for a יבמה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finds a limiting word in the גט verse: 'לה' teaches that a גט works for a wife and not for a יבמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'for her.' 'For her' means a גט works for her, but not for a יבמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by finding a limiting word in the תורה, the same kind of exclusion the ברייתא used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 26 showed that only a limiting verse can block a קל וחומר. So the גמרא points to 'לה' in the גט passage. That word limits the גט to a married woman, which excludes a יבמה.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse says
'For her' (from 'וכתב לה ספר כריתת')
A widow waiting for יבום or חליצה from her late husband's brother

phrases.english: The verse says: 'for her';
phrases.notes: דברים 24:1 and 24:3: 'וכתב לה ספר כריתת', 'and he writes for her a document of severance.'

phrases.english: 'for her', but not for a יבמה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 26 by supplying a limiting verse, as the ברייתא did.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New source: a limiting word in the verse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without a limiting verse, the reverse קל וחומר would let a גט release a יבמה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לה' limits the גט to a married woman, so it does not work for a יבמה.

steps.title: Maybe 'לה' means 'for her sake'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that 'לה' is needed to teach that a גט must be written for this woman's sake.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that 'for her' means it must be written for her sake!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 27 by giving 'לה' a different job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'לה' teaches that a גט must be written for the specific woman, it is already used up. Then it cannot also exclude a יבמה.

keyTerms.meaning: But say instead
For her sake: written specifically for this woman

phrases.english: But say that 'for her' means for her sake!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of 'לה' in step 27.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word is needed for the rule of לשמה, so it is not free to teach anything else.

steps.title: 'לה' is written twice
steps.stepSummary: There are two appearances of 'לה', so one can teach לשמה and the other can exclude a יבמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'For her' is written twice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word appears twice, so there is room for both lessons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One 'לה' teaches that the גט must be written for her sake. The second 'לה' is free to teach that a גט does not work for a יבמה.

keyTerms.meaning: Two
Are written

phrases.english: 'For her' is written twice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 28 by pointing out that the word appears twice.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra word in the verse, so both lessons can be learned
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A single 'לה' would be used up by לשמה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two 'לה's: one for לשמה, one to exclude a יבמה.

steps.title: The second 'לה' is also needed: one גט cannot serve two women
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that the second 'לה' is needed too, to teach that one גט cannot be used for two women. So there is still no word left to exclude a יבמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But still, one 'for her' is needed to teach 'for her sake,' and the other 'for her' is needed to teach: for her, and not for her and her co-wife!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 29: both appearances of 'לה' already have jobs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first 'לה' teaches לשמה. The second teaches that one גט cannot divorce two women at once. That leaves no extra word to exclude a יבמה, so the גמרא needs a new source. Step 31 brings one.

keyTerms.meaning: And still / but even so
It is needed for (a different lesson)
And the other one
Her co-wife (another wife of the same husband)

phrases.english: But still, it is needed:
one 'for her' for her sake,
and the other 'for her':
and not for her and her co-wife!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer in step 29 by assigning the second 'לה' its own lesson.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 29 that the second 'לה' is free to exclude a יבמה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both 'לה's are already used: one for לשמה, one to rule out a single גט for two women. Nothing is left to exclude a יבמה.

steps.title: Only a shoe releases a יבמה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the 'לה' approach. It brings a new source: the word 'נעל' teaches that a יבמה is released only through the shoe of חליצה, not through anything else such as a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the verse says 'shoe.' A shoe, yes; anything else, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The 'לה' answer has collapsed, so the גמרא gives a brand-new source for why a גט cannot release a יבמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about חליצה speaks specifically of a shoe. The גמרא reads that as a limit: the release must come through the shoe of חליצה. That shuts out a גט, so the קל וחומר from an ordinary wife is blocked by this verse.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the earlier approach is dropped and a new one is coming.
The verse says. It introduces a source from the תורה.
Shoe. This is the shoe removed at חליצה.
Something else.

phrases.english: Rather, the verse says:
"Shoe": a shoe, yes,
phrases.notes: דברים 25:10

phrases.english: something else, no.
phrases.notes: He means a גט is one of those 'something else' things, so it cannot release her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the 'לה' source, which Step 30 showed was fully used up, with a new limiting word.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without a limiting word, a קל וחומר from an ordinary wife would let a גט release a יבמה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'נעל' limits the release of a יבמה to חליצה alone, so a גט does not work.

steps.title: The word 'shoe' is already needed elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether 'נעל' is really free to teach this. It quotes a ברייתא that uses the repeated word 'נעל' to include anyone's shoe for חליצה, not just the man's own.
steps.simpleTranslation: But does this word 'shoe' come to teach that? It is needed for what a ברייתא teaches: 'his shoe.' From that I would know only his own shoe. From where do we know the shoe of any person? The verse says 'shoe' and again 'shoe,' which includes it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new source. It says the word 'נעל' is already busy teaching a different law about חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא reads 'נעלו' (his shoe) and asks how we know someone else's shoe also works. It answers from the word 'נעל' written twice, which widens the law to include any shoe. If 'נעל' is used up for that, it cannot also exclude a גט.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for something else.
As a ברייתא teaches.
His shoe.
The verse comes to teach.
It included. The verse widened the law.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'נעל' (a shoe, any shoe) with 'נעלו' (his shoe). The ברייתא builds its law on the difference between these two words.

phrases.english: But this word "shoe"
does it come for this?
It is needed
for that which is taught in a ברייתא:
"His shoe": I would know only his own shoe;
phrases.notes: דברים 25:9

phrases.aramaic: נַעַל שֶׁל כׇּל אָדָם מְנָא לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: the shoe of any person, from where do we know it?
The verse says "shoe," "shoe": this includes it.
phrases.notes: The word 'shoe' shows up in two verses, and that extra mention widens the law to any shoe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 31 by showing that its source word is already used for another law.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of 'נעל' to exclude a גט for a יבמה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A word cannot teach two things. The ברייתא needs 'נעל' to include anyone's shoe, so the word is not free to exclude a גט.

steps.title: 'His shoe' means a shoe that fits him
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. Since any shoe works, the word 'נעלו' must teach that the shoe has to fit the man. A shoe too big to walk in or too small to cover most of the foot does not work. The list continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the verse say 'his shoe'? It means his shoe that is fit for him. That excludes a shoe so big he cannot walk in it, and a shoe so small it does not cover most of his foot, and excludes...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting the same ברייתא. It explains what the word 'נעלו' teaches, now that 'נעל' has already included anyone's shoe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once any shoe is allowed, 'his shoe' cannot mean ownership. So the ברייתא reads it as 'a shoe suited to him,' and that rules out shoes that are too large or too small. This shows that both 'נעל' and 'נעלו' are being used, which strengthens the challenge of Step 32.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the ברייתא brought in Step 32 and explains what the word 'נעלו' teaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The shoe used for חליצה must fit the man. A shoe too big to walk in or too small to cover most of his foot is excluded.
